title: Identifiability of Noise Sources in Bodily Judgments
subtitle: A computational audit of parietal stimulation and a conditional paired-readout design
author: Hongju Liu
decision_scope: Internal scientific/editorial readiness after AI-assisted technical reviews and the user's explicit instruction to complete and release this paper. This is not external peer review, journal acceptance, final human line-by-line review, empirical protocol validation, or evidence that any external release operation has succeeded.
revision_relation: Prepares the first public CTD edition from the archived unpublished v0.1 and v0.2 research records. Their original metadata and numerical evidence remain unchanged. Does not amend the published SCU preprint.

net_contribution.claim: The released information-criterion rows match a second negation of positive NLL. The corrected aggregate still favors Sigma.
A conditional signed-SOA symmetry diagnostic rejects the centered independent-binomial family without fitting its parameters.
A corrected fixed within-cell five-fold comparison favors Sigma plus task-specific centers over Prior plus task-specific centers, conditional on these retrospective families.
An explicit fixed-sensory, variable-criterion implementation preserves all 1,260 source marginal probabilities while retaining the source threshold policy.

One additional population joint probability identifies shared Gaussian variance under calibrated centers and independent criteria/lapses; bounded criterion correlation yields a sharp set and central weak identification is quantified.

A CP probability interval is projected through the complete calibrated paired Gaussian model, covering the whole population variance set at nominal finite-sample probability; sharp endpoints, empty/full-domain cases and unequal variances are explicit.

An honest complete nuisance-calibration union yields at least 1-alpha-gamma coverage; exact finite unions and continuous kappa-only uncertainty are implemented without pretending to solve arbitrary continuous multi-parameter regions.

Exact finite-binomial sums over 480 fixed scenarios retain every profile. All 240 valid cases meet nominal 95% coverage, with often-wide sets; controls expose incorrect physical attribution and explicit target-role changes. No new human data or Monte Carlo draws.

inherited_material: Gaussian addition of independent variances and sensory/criterion ambiguity (including Yarrow et al.).
Bias and decision strategy in simultaneity judgments (Cabrera et al.; Yarrow et al.).
BCI accounts of ownership and sensory uncertainty (Chancel et al.; D’Angelo et al.).
Bivariate normal derivative identities (Plackett) and the general principle that extra measurements can aid noise identification.
The SCU distinction between matching behavior and verified source use; CTD v0.1 descriptive width results.
Clopper and Pearson (1934), DOI 10.1093/biomet/26.4.404: inherited exact binomial confidence interval.
Classical confidence-set projection, event intersection and the union bound; these are proved for the explicit observer rather than claimed as new general principles.
priority_status: No claim of a new general confidence-interval framework, Gaussian decomposition principle, shortest confidence set or universally first discovery. The auditable source-specific combination and conditional finite-sample application are proposed contributions; exhaustive priority is unverified.

seven_questions.precise_problem: When can a condition-dependent response curve identify a sensory source, and what additional calibrated paired measurement and finite-sample uncertainty are needed when marginally equivalent decision implementations exist?
seven_questions.citable_increment: Source-specific IC reconciliation, centering failure, transparent restricted predictive comparison, exact source-family counterpart, conditional paired inverse and sharp correlation bound, with an executable finite-sample confidence procedure and fixed operating-characteristic study.
seven_questions.nearest_prior_art: The manuscript credits D'Angelo et al., Chancel et al., Yarrow et al., Cabrera et al., Plackett and Clopper-Pearson. Final source/novelty review qualifies priority. Gaussian noise addition, joint-response inference and confidence projection are inherited.
seven_questions.testable_scope: Released aggregate count cells and explicitly declared independent-binomial/Gaussian families. Prospective paired inference requires actual common-sample routing, calibrated centers, joint Gaussian criteria independent of sensory noise, known independent lapse processes, a justified covariance bound and iid fixed-n pairs.
seven_questions.reproduction: Three unchanged public workbooks, licensed source-code snapshots, full fits/partitions, source audits, exact population proofs, fixed finite-sample plan, confidence tables, operating-characteristic outputs, independent internal checks, superseded failures and correction receipts are retained.
seven_questions.future_reuse: An investigator can audit a fitted response family, construct a marginal counterpart, identify missing joint information, quantify its calibrated confidence set and expose how violated consumer/lapse assumptions invalidate physical attribution.
seven_questions.position_and_preservation: One methods and retrospective secondary-analysis preprint is ready for authorized release. v0.1/v0.2 evidence remains historical and unchanged; CTD2/CTD3 candidates stay disabled. External publication and persistence are separate coordinator-verified steps.
